subject: W1-DEPLOY r2 — re-take the score on the deploy-safety instruments after the r1 fixes and the new tools landed
predecessor: critic-w1-deploy (r1, score 3.5, FAIL); critic-w1-deploy-r2 attempt 1 (killed by the usage limit, no artifacts on disk — its status file's next_step was still 'verify the landings from git log', so this run started from there rather than re-claiming finished work)
headline: The score did not move — 3.5 to 3.5 — and that is a coincidence, not a stasis. The axis that SET r1's 3.5 (check-shipped-files.mjs) improved to 4.5: its self-test now genuinely executes the scanner and its rule-13 blast radius is fixed and measured correct. The 3.5 is now set by three NEW findings. (1) verify-playable --self-test FAILS on the shipped tree because its own control is red, and the cause is the instrument: it takes a full-page screenshot every 2 s while timing the boot it is judging, and the observed arm is slower in 3 of 3 paired runs (10.7s vs 69.7s, 14.5s vs 48.4s, 52.4s vs 72.3s) with 3 of 6 screenshots timing out. (2) The boot notice's new 20 s hard ceiling erases its own black-screen diagnosis at 19.7 s — accused at 5.7 s, gone at 19.7 s, and with the ceiling deleted still on the glass at 45 s, so the control is not inert. It also deletes the signal verify-playable reads as 'the page's own verdict on itself'. (3) verify-live-site's staleness check hashes the deployed bytes against the WORKING TREE rather than HEAD (3 of 60 sampled files differ from the worktree, 0 from HEAD) and looks at 2 of 715 files, while printing 'the deployed bytes match what we published'.

commits_measured_at.check-shipped-files.mjs: worktree sha256 54bb8dab2962 (GATE-BLAST-RADIUS's new version, uncommitted at measurement time) AND sha256 f611eb7def40 (the previous one, via r1's own fixture)

PLAYABILITY owns verify-playable.mjs and game/index.html; GATE-BLAST-RADIUS owns check-shipped-files.mjs, tools/bank.mjs and .githooks/pre-commit; P10-loader-retry owns loader-retry.mjs. None of those files was written by this critic. GATE-BLAST-RADIUS moved to `done` DURING this round and its new gate landed in the worktree mid-measurement, so the verdict reports BOTH versions of the gate and says which is which. tools/scores.mjs was not declared in advance: it was edited because publish.mjs fails closed on an unmapped piece and would otherwise have left the progress page without the new number, which is the whole point of this dispatch. The reason is written into the file at the edit, next to the four identical notes other critics left there.
could_not_do: Did not reproduce the bank.mjs unstage-on-false-positive on the live tree: planting a `?v=` import under game/ would have dropped a neighbour's file out of the next bank. scan()'s half is reproduced in a throwaway repository and the unstage is four lines further on, quoted in the verdict.
The observer-effect figures are 3 paired reps, not a distribution. The effect is 1.4x-6.5x and present in all three, and it shrinks as background load rises because the box then dominates.

verify-playable --self-test was run in --local, not the documented default --live. The live mirror fetches ~700 files down one CONNECT tunnel each, which would have made the observer-effect attribution harder, not easier.

The --play leg of verify-playable was not exercised at all. It is the newest and least-graded part of the family and the only thing in it that asserts the game can be STARTED. It needs its own round and is named in the verdict.
No figure anywhere is from a real phone or a real network. That limit belongs to the whole family; live-mirror.mjs states it plainly, which is the right way to carry it.

The corpus has no deployment or shipping reference item (no RI-DEP, RI-SHIP, RI-PLAY), so the seven axes are named by this critic rather than by an item. RI-MTH04 is carried in spirit and marked `measured: partial`. Raised as an arbitration_question in the verdict rather than papered over.
